# Decision memo (board, decide mode)

A board-style decision record. The skill fills this and appends it to the venture's `Administration/Decisions.md` (or, for a cross-venture call with no venture record, files it where the repository's instructions keep reports or at the path the user names, and otherwise returns it in chat), then adds a one-line entry to the venture's `Log.md`. Lead with the answer; preserve the minority view. The convened functions and chiefs are derived from the brief, not fixed.

**Decision requested:** [the question, in one line]
**Recommendation (BLUF):** [the call, stated first, with the one accountable owner named]
**Decider:** [CEO for a reversible, in-mandate call; Founder for an irreversible or major one]
**Status:** [decided | escalated | revisit]

## Situation and complication

[the shared context, what changed, and why the call is live now]

## The question

[the exact choice, at the right altitude, with the decision criteria]

## Options considered

[each option scored against the criteria; include the option not taken and why]

| Option | [criterion] | [criterion] | [criterion] | Net |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [A] |  |  |  |  |
| [B] |  |  |  |  |

## Each function's view and the tradeoffs

[one line per convened function (only the ones the decision touched), each with the tradeoff it raised]

- **[Function] ([chief]):** [view; the tradeoff it sees]
- **[Function] ([chief]):** [view; any Agree or veto threshold]

## Risks and pre-mortem

[the major risks rated by likelihood and impact, with mitigations; the pre-mortem causes, the ways this fails a year out]

## Decision and owner

[the call, the decider, and the one accountable owner; note any escalation to the Founder]

## Next steps

- [action] - [owner] - [date]

## Minority view

[the dissent, by role and reason; present even when the call is confident. A hard call with no recorded dissent usually means it was smoothed over, not that it was absent.]
board.templates/deliverable-contract.md:
# Deliverable contract (the output contract every operate deliverable carries)

*The header every OPERATE artifact ships with before it lands: what it is, who owns it, where it is filed, the Definition of Done it was built against, the verifier's sign-off, and whether it is Founder-gated. The lead fills this from the brief, the Head of Quality signs it, and the skill (the sole writer) lands it. No agent writes; agents compose and return, the skill persists.*

This is the producing-side twin of `templates/board-brief.md` (which frames a decide run). A board brief frames a question; a deliverable contract frames a produced artifact and travels with it from the lead's brief, through the Head of Quality's verification, to the write-gate. One contract per artifact. A request that needs three artifacts is three contracts, sequenced on their dependencies (`references/deliverable-dependency-chains.md`). The contract is what makes the producer-to-artifact handoff checkable end to end: a deliverable with no owning file and no Definition of Done is not producible, and the verifier returns it unbuilt.

Read this with `references/specialist-dispatch.md` (the produce loop that fills it), `references/department-deliverable-catalog.md` (the per-function owning file and DoD), `references/verification.md` (how the Head of Quality checks the DoD), and `references/write-gate.md` (the green and red lanes the gate field maps to). The owning-file names and the DoD lines below are drawn from the catalog; keep them in sync with it, never invent a new owning file here.

## The contract (fill one per artifact)

```
ARTIFACT:        [the specific deliverable, named, not a capability. "Q3 3-statement model", not "finance work".]
OWNING DEPT:     [the workforce function that owns it, e.g. Finance and Accounting (F&A).]
LEAD (owner):    [the one accountable lead, e.g. Chief Financial Officer. One name. This is the accountable owner of record.]
SPECIALIST(S):   [the producer(s) the lead dispatched, e.g. FP&A Analyst. Who built it, for the record.]
FILED TO:        [the single <Dept>/ file of the venture's record it lands in, from the catalog. e.g. F&A/Financial-Model.md.]
TRIGGER:         [what called for it: a planning cycle, a raise, a launch, a review run, a stage change.]
STAGE:           [found | scale | maintain. Scales the rigor: a Seed model is a driver-based projection, not an audit-grade build.]
LADDERS TO:      [the strategy objective or OKR in Strategy.md / Goals.md this serves, so nothing is built unmoored.]
DEPENDS ON:      [the upstream artifacts it builds on, if any (e.g. positioning before GTM); none if it is a root artifact.]

DEFINITION OF DONE (the bar the Head of Quality checks, from the catalog):
  - [checkable condition 1]
  - [checkable condition 2]
  - [checkable condition 3]

COMPLETION EVIDENCE (returned with the artifact; the verifier checks the evidence, not the claim):
  - [every number traced to a source, a tool call, or a venture file; every assumption named.]

VERIFIER SIGN-OFF (Head of Quality):
  - Result:     [ cleared | cleared with noted defects | returned | escalated ]
  - Checked:    [the specific evidence checked, not a general thumbs-up.]
  - Defects:    [any noted gaps or open questions that travel with the artifact; none if clean.]

FOUNDER-GATED:   [no | yes - <which red category>. A "no" means the skill writes it autonomously into the venture folder
                  once verified, with the prior state committed. A "yes" means the skill prepares the action and stops for the Founder's
                  explicit confirmation. The five red categories are fixed (write-gate.md): moving money, signing or
                  sending a contract, publishing or sending external comms, deleting a file, changing equity or the cap
                  table. When in doubt, gated.]

WRITE-BACK:      [the Log.md line the skill appends, and any Goals.md / Overview.md stage update the artifact triggers.]
```

## How each field is set, and by whom

- **Artifact, owning dept, filed-to, DoD** come straight from `references/department-deliverable-catalog.md`. The catalog is the source of truth for which file each artifact lands in and what its DoD is; the contract copies them, it does not redefine them. If the catalog has no owning file for the artifact, the artifact is not yet producible, and that is a finding, not a thing to invent a home for.
- **Lead and specialist(s)** come from the catalog's function entry. The lead is the single accountable owner; the specialists are the producers the lead dispatched (`references/specialist-dispatch.md`). The lead frames and approves and never types the artifact; the specialist builds it; neither one writes the file.
- **Stage and ladders-to** come from the venture-context preflight: the chair read `Overview.md`, `Goals.md`, `Strategy.md`, and recent `Log.md`, and detected the stage (`references/lifecycle.md`). The stage scales the rigor and the catalog subset; ladders-to keeps the artifact tied to a real objective so the work is not unmoored.
- **Completion evidence** is the producer's, returned with the artifact. The rule is `references/verification.md`'s: every number, every named fact, every external claim traces to a tool call, a venture file, or a cited source. Nothing load-bearing rests on recall.
- **Verifier sign-off** is the Head of Quality's alone. A producer never verifies its own work. The Head of Quality receives the artifact, this contract, and the claimed sources in a fresh worker that holds none of the producer's reasoning, and checks the artifact against the DoD and the evidence. The four results are `cleared`, `cleared with noted defects`, `returned`, `escalated` (`references/verification.md`). A `returned` artifact does not land; it goes back to the lead with the specific finding. Consequential output does not land unverified.
- **Founder-gated** maps to the write-gate's two lanes (`references/write-gate.md`). Green (autonomous): internal, reversible drafts and models into the venture's own folder, written once verified, with the prior state committed. Red (hard-gated): the five fixed categories, which never go autonomous at any stage or tier; a CEO-seat yes is advice, not authorization. Stage moves the dollar line inside the green lane, never the category line.
- **Write-back** is what the skill does after the gate clears: persist the artifact into the filed-to file (with an existing file's last state committed first), append a dated line to the venture `Log.md`, and update `Goals.md` or the `Overview.md` stage when they changed. Then run the checks the repository's instructions name.

## The gate the contract walks before it is written

The skill walks the write-gate checklist (`references/write-gate.md`) against this contract, in order, and stops at the first red:

1. **Is the FOUNDER-GATED field a red category?** (money, contract, external comms, delete, equity or cap table.) Yes - frame the action, state it, get the Founder's explicit confirmation. Do not proceed on a CEO-seat yes.
2. **Does it cross outside this venture's folder, or is it irreversible?** Yes - same as above.
3. **Does the implied spend or hire exceed the stage threshold** (`assets/delegation-of-authority.json`)? The artifact is green to draft; the action is red to execute. Gate the action.
4. **Green so far - is the existing file's last state committed?** No - commit it first. A new file needs nothing.
5. **Is the output consequential, and has the Head of Quality cleared it?** Consequential and unverified does not pass, even when reversible. Verify first.
6. **All clear - write it.** Persist, append to `Log.md`, update `Goals.md` / `Overview.md` if changed, then run the checks the repository's instructions name.

---

## Per-department artifact stubs (the highest-value contracts, pre-filled)

Four worked stubs, one per common producing department, with the owning file and DoD already drawn from `references/department-deliverable-catalog.md`. Copy the relevant stub into a fresh contract, fill the brackets from the venture, and let the body of the artifact follow the stub's structure. These are the artifacts an operate run produces most; the full per-function catalog is in `references/department-deliverable-catalog.md`.

### Stub A - PRD / product spec (R&D)

```
ARTIFACT:        [feature or product name] PRD
OWNING DEPT:     Research and Development (R&D)
LEAD (owner):    Chief Product Officer
SPECIALIST(S):   Product Manager (the what and why); Applied Researcher (the validating evidence)
FILED TO:        R&D/Roadmap.md   (the GTM surface for the same product lands in S&M/Products.md)
TRIGGER:         a build is greenlit
STAGE:           [scale, typically]
LADDERS TO:      [the strategy objective in Strategy.md / the OKR in Goals.md this build serves]
DEPENDS ON:      user-research synthesis and the MRD (the evidence the requirements rest on)
DEFINITION OF DONE:
  - the requirement ties to a strategy objective in Strategy.md or Goals.md
  - each requirement has acceptance criteria a verifier can check (testable, not aspirational)
  - the validated and invalidated assumptions are recorded; an invalidated assumption is kept, not quietly dropped
  - the engineering contract is unambiguous: scope in, scope out, and the go / no-go gates named
FOUNDER-GATED:   no  (an internal spec; the build it authorizes may carry gated spend, checked separately)
```

Body sections: problem and the evidence for it; the user and the job-to-be-done; goals and non-goals; requirements with acceptance criteria; the assumptions (validated and invalidated); dependencies and the release gates; the metric that will tell us it worked (defined in Metrics.md, not redefined here).

### Stub B - SOP / runbook (O&L)

```
ARTIFACT:        [process name] SOP
OWNING DEPT:     Operations and Logistics (O&L)
LEAD (owner):    Head of Operations
SPECIALIST(S):   Process Analyst (maps and improves the process)
FILED TO:        O&L/Operations.md
TRIGGER:         a process that lives in one head, an audit, or a handoff that keeps breaking
STAGE:           [scale or maintain]
LADDERS TO:      [the operating objective or the reliability / cycle-time target this procedure serves]
DEPENDS ON:      none (or the upstream process it hands off from)
DEFINITION OF DONE:
  - every step is executable as written (a stranger to the process can run it)
  - The RACI names real owners, not placeholders
  - the exception and rollback paths exist and are reachable from the happy path
  - each KPI the SOP is measured by has a definition, a target band, and a current value (referencing Metrics.md)
FOUNDER-GATED:   no  (committing vendor spend or signing a supplier contract surfaced by the SOP is red, gated separately)
```

Body sections: purpose and scope; the trigger and the inputs; the RACI; the step-by-step procedure (a flowchart where it helps); the exception paths and the rollback; the KPIs and their target bands; the review cadence and the owner.

### Stub C - GTM one-pager (S&M)

```
ARTIFACT:        [product or launch name] GTM one-pager
OWNING DEPT:     Sales and Marketing (S&M)
LEAD (owner):    Chief Revenue Officer
SPECIALIST(S):   Product Marketing Manager (positioning, launch); Demand Generation Manager (the channel and pipeline plan)
FILED TO:        S&M/Products.md   (the offer detail lands in S&M/Services.md; positioning lives in S&M/Brand.md)
TRIGGER:         a launch or a new market
STAGE:           [found for a founder-led GTM note; scale for the repeatable motion]
LADDERS TO:      [the growth OKR in Goals.md this launch serves]
DEPENDS ON:      the positioning and brand guide in S&M/Brand.md (positioning precedes GTM)
DEFINITION OF DONE:
  - The ICP is specific (not "everyone"); the segment is named and bounded
  - the why-now is evidenced, not asserted
  - launch tiers have owners and dates
  - the pipeline target and the channel mix are stated and traceable to a number
  - any published external asset is flagged Founder-gated, never sent autonomously
FOUNDER-GATED:   the plan: no.  any external publication or send it produces: yes - publishing or sending external comms.
```

Body sections (one page): ICP and the job-to-be-done; the why-now; how-we-win (the wedge against alternatives); the offer and pricing surface; launch tiers with owners and dates; the channel mix and the pipeline target; the metric that defines a successful launch (from Metrics.md).

### Stub D - Compensation bands (HR)

```
ARTIFACT:        Compensation bands - [scope: a level, a function, or company-wide]
OWNING DEPT:     Human Resources (HR)
LEAD (owner):    Chief Human Resources Officer
SPECIALIST(S):   a compensation seat spawned on demand (the benchmarked ranges and the rewards mix)
FILED TO:        HR/Hierarchy.md
TRIGGER:         a hiring wave or an annual compensation review
STAGE:           [scale, typically]
LADDERS TO:      [the org-design objective in Strategy.md; costed against the runway in F&A/Financial-Model.md]
DEPENDS ON:      the org design and the role charters in HR/Hierarchy.md; the runway in F&A/Financial-Model.md
DEFINITION OF DONE:
  - each band is benchmarked to a named source and stated as a range, not a point
  - the equity guidelines and the approval workflow are stated
  - the plan is costed against Financial-Model.md runway, not set in a vacuum
  - no real person's actual compensation or termination is decided here (those escalate to the Founder)
FOUNDER-GATED:   the bands: no.  an actual offer drawn from them: yes - it commits money and is a contract.
```

Body sections: the leveling framework (the ladder the bands sit on); the benchmark source and its vintage; the bands by level and function (range, not point); the equity and total-rewards guidelines; the approval workflow; the runway cost of filling the open plan at band midpoint.

---

## The standard the contract holds

One contract, one artifact, one owning file, one accountable lead, one verifier's sign-off, one writer. **Every angle heard in producing it, one owner accountable for it.** The lead frames and approves; the specialists produce in isolation and never grade their own work; the Head of Quality verifies independently against the DoD; the skill alone writes, behind the write-gate. The contract is stage-aware (the rigor and the catalog subset scale to found, scale, or maintain), grounded (every number traces, the artifact ladders to a real objective), and gated (the five red categories are the Founder's alone to authorize). A deliverable that cannot fill this contract is not done, and the skill does not write a deliverable the verifier returned.

See `references/specialist-dispatch.md` for the produce loop that fills the contract, `references/verification.md` for the sign-off discipline, `references/write-gate.md` for the gate the FOUNDER-GATED field maps to, and `references/department-deliverable-catalog.md` for the owning file and DoD of every other artifact.
board.templates/founding-checklist.md:
# Founding checklist - the gated idea-to-launch scaffold for FOUND mode

*The seven-stage, gated checklist a found run works through: validate, MVP, incorporate, equity, GTM, hire, raise. Each stage carries a go/no-go gate that must clear before the next stage opens, and the two irreversible founding clocks (the 83(b) 30-day window and the QSBS 5-year hold) are flagged hard at the top and again at the stage that starts them. This is a working scaffold: copy it into the new venture and fill the brackets. The chair runs the stages in order; the skill writes the results back behind the write-gate (see write-gate.md), and the standing FOUND-stage doctrine that scales the run is in lifecycle.md.*

Stage and rigor for everything below come from lifecycle.md (FOUND, Idea to Seed): protect runway and learning velocity, resist premature process and premature hiring, and run the smallest sufficient roster (often the chair, who holds strategy framing, plus the CFO, and the CRO on a first-customer question). The dominant question of the whole stage is one line: **is there real evidence of product-market fit?** Every gate below is a way of asking it again at higher resolution. The chair holds the question, the convened functions form independent views, the Head of Quality verifies anything consequential before it lands, and the skill is the sole writer. Every angle heard, one owner accountable.

How to read a gate: a gate is a **go / no-go / pivot** decision, not a checkbox. A `no-go` stops the stage and protects runway; a `pivot` resets the loop with a changed assumption (Build-Measure-Learn); a `go` opens the next stage. Run each gate as a small decide pass (see deliberation.md) and record the call to the venture's `Log.md`. Do not let a stage's tasks open before its predecessor's gate has cleared. Found is sequential by design; the gates are where the venture earns the right to spend the next dollar.

---

## ⚠️ HARD-DEADLINE FLAGS - read first, these clocks do not pause

Two founding actions start irreversible legal clocks. Missing either is expensive and usually uncurable. Both are **red / Founder-gated** actions (changing equity or the cap table, see write-gate.md); the skill drafts and models them, the Founder executes them, and the deadline is logged the day the clock starts.

- [ ] 🚩 **83(b) election - file within 30 DAYS of the stock grant. No extensions, ever.** When a founder receives restricted stock subject to vesting, an 83(b) election tells the IRS to tax the equity at grant (when it is worth ~nothing) rather than as it vests (when it may be worth a great deal). The window is **30 calendar days from the grant date**, it cannot be extended, and a missed election can create a large ordinary-income tax bill on paper gains the founder never received in cash. Action: at incorporation, the moment founder stock is issued, record the **grant date** here → `[grant date]`, the **filing deadline (grant + 30 days)** → `[grant date + 30]`, and confirm each founder mails their election (certified, return receipt). Owner: General Counsel drafts; **Founder signs and mails.** This is the single most time-sensitive item in the entire founding process.
- [ ] 🚩 **QSBS - the 5-YEAR holding clock starts at original issuance.** Qualified Small Business Stock (Section 1202) can exempt a large share of the gain from federal tax on a later sale, but only if the stock is **held for at least 5 years** from the date it was originally issued, and only if the company qualified at issuance (a domestic C-corp, gross assets under the cap at and just after issuance, an active qualified trade or business). The clock does not start at sale or at a round; it starts at **original issuance**. Action: record the **issuance date** here → `[issuance date]` and the **5-year maturity date** → `[issuance date + 5 years]`, and confirm the entity is a C-corp at issuance (the LLC path forfeits QSBS, see Incorporate). Owner: CFO tracks the clock; General Counsel confirms qualification. Flagging it now protects an exit five years out.

> Both clocks are set in the **Incorporate** and **Equity** stages below. They are surfaced here at the top because by the time they are visible in the workflow it is often already too late. If a found run opens with stock already granted, the chair's first move is to check the 83(b) window before anything else.

---

## Stage 1 - VALIDATE (riskiest assumption first)

*Find real, urgent demand before building anything. The product is a hypothesis; the customer is the experiment. Output: a lean canvas, evidence from real conversations, and a single named riskiest assumption that the next stages are built to retire.*

Convene: chair (CEO, wearing the strategy hat) on the thesis, CRO (with the Product Marketing Manager) on the customer. Roster stays small (lifecycle.md, FOUND).

- [ ] Name the **single riskiest unvalidated assumption** in one sentence → `[the one thing that, if false, kills this]`. Everything downstream tests it.
- [ ] Draft the **lean canvas**: problem, customer segment, unique value proposition, solution, channels, revenue streams, cost structure, key metrics, unfair advantage. File to `Administration/Strategy.md` (the thesis the OKRs will ladder up to).
- [ ] Identify and reach the **first 10 target customers** (named, not personas) → `[list]`. Daily founder-led outreach (lifecycle.md cadence).
- [ ] Run **problem-validation interviews** (aim for 15 to 30): is the problem real, urgent, and currently being paid for in time or money? Record raw notes, not summaries that flatter the idea.
- [ ] Test **willingness to pay** with a real ask (a pre-order, a letter of intent, a paid pilot, a deposit). A "yes I'd use that" is not evidence; a card on file or a signed LOI is.
- [ ] Confirm **founder-market fit**: why this team for this problem, what unfair insight or access they hold → `[the unfair advantage]`.
- [ ] Map the **competitive and substitute landscape** (including "do nothing" and the spreadsheet they use today). Thin is fine here; honest is required.

> **Metrics that count (and the ones that do not).** Count: interviews completed, willingness-to-pay signals, problem-validation rate, early activation among any pilots. Suppress as not-yet-applicable (lifecycle.md, metrics-and-kpis.md): Rule of 40, Magic Number, CAC payback, NRR. Revenue here is a lagging vanity signal; do not report it as a headline.

### 🚦 GATE 1 - Problem/solution evidence

- [ ] **Go:** real, urgent problem confirmed by independent customers, a credible willingness-to-pay signal, and founder-market fit. → opens **MVP**.
- [ ] **Pivot:** the problem is real but the segment, value proposition, or willingness-to-pay is wrong. Reset the canvas, change the assumption, re-run the loop. Record what changed.
- [ ] **No-go:** no urgent problem, or no one will pay. Stop and protect runway. A clean no-go here is the cheapest decision the venture will ever make.

Record the gate call to `Log.md` (decision, rationale, owner, the assumption it retired or exposed).

---

## Stage 2 - MVP (build the smallest thing that produces learning)

*Build the minimum that lets a real customer get real value and lets you measure whether they come back. The goal is learning velocity, not feature completeness. Output: a working MVP in the hands of the first customers, and the first cohort-retention signal.*

Convene: chair + R&D (the Chief Product Officer / the Product Manager on the what, the Applied Researcher on the build) + the CRO's marketing seat (Product Marketing Manager) on early customers. Resist premature process: no SOPs for a thing that does not yet work (lifecycle.md).

- [ ] Write a **one-page MVP definition**: the single core job the MVP does, and the explicit list of what it deliberately does **not** do yet. File to `Research & Development (R&D)/Products.md`.
- [ ] Define the **Build-Measure-Learn loop**: the hypothesis, the metric that confirms or refutes it, and the smallest build that tests it. Weekly BML standup (lifecycle.md cadence).
- [ ] Define **activation** ("first value") precisely → `[the moment a user first gets the core value]`, and instrument it.
- [ ] Ship the MVP to the **first paying or design-partner customers** (the 10 from Stage 1 where possible).
- [ ] Measure **cohort retention** and **meaningful (not vanity) usage**: do they come back, and do they do the core action again without prompting?
- [ ] Capture **qualitative feedback** at the point of use; sort signal (a pattern across customers) from noise (one loud voice).
- [ ] Decide **pivot or persevere** after each loop, on evidence, not attachment.

> Stay reversible and fast: FOUND favors a quick reversible decision over a slow perfect one (lifecycle.md, rigor). A pre-mortem on the one riskiest assumption beats a full dissent battery at this stage.

### 🚦 GATE 2 - First signs of retention (the PMF gate at low resolution)

- [ ] **Go:** an MVP that delivers the core value, a defined activation event customers reach, and an early cohort-retention signal (some cohort comes back). → opens **Incorporate**.
- [ ] **Pivot:** customers activate but do not return, or the core job is wrong. Change the product hypothesis, not the customer's mind. Reset the BML loop.
- [ ] **No-go:** no path to retention after honest iteration. Stop or pivot hard. Building more features is not the fix for a missing why.

Record to `Log.md`.

---

## Stage 3 - INCORPORATE (form the entity, set both founding clocks)

*Stand up the legal entity, and with it the two irreversible clocks. This stage is where the 83(b) window opens and the QSBS clock starts. The default is a Delaware C-corp when a venture-capital track is realistic; the LLC path is the explicit deviation for a lifestyle or cash-flow business and forfeits QSBS. Output: a formed entity, an EIN, a bank account, founding agreements, and both deadline clocks set on the record.*

Convene: chair + General Counsel (the General Counsel / the Commercial Counsel) + CFO. Entity choice and equity are **red / Founder-gated** (write-gate.md): the team drafts and models, the Founder signs.

- [ ] Decide and record the **entity type** → `[Delaware C-corp | LLC | other]`. **Default: Delaware C-corp** if a VC raise is realistically on the table (clean for priced rounds, SAFEs, options, and QSBS). **LLC** is the explicit deviation for a lifestyle/cash-flow venture and **forfeits QSBS eligibility** (QSBS requires a C-corp at issuance). Owner: General Counsel recommends; **Founder decides.**
- [ ] File the **certificate of incorporation**; adopt **bylaws** and the **initial board consent**. File the entity-formation pack to `Legal & Compliance (L&C)/Compliance.md`.
- [ ] Obtain the **EIN** (federal tax id) → `[EIN]`.
- [ ] Open the **business bank account** (separate from personal funds from day one; commingling pierces the liability shield).
- [ ] Execute **founding agreements**: founders' agreement, IP and invention assignment (every founder assigns all relevant IP to the company), and any cofounder vesting terms. IP assignment is not optional; unassigned founder IP is a fatal diligence flag later.
- [ ] Issue **founder restricted stock** and record the **grant date** → `[grant date]`. **This starts the 83(b) 30-day clock and the QSBS 5-year clock.**
- [ ] 🚩 **Set the 83(b) deadline now:** grant + 30 days → `[grant date + 30]`. Each founder files (certified mail, return receipt). Owner: General Counsel drafts; **Founder signs and mails within 30 days. No extensions.**
- [ ] 🚩 **Set the QSBS clock now:** issuance date → `[issuance date]`; 5-year maturity → `[issuance date + 5 years]`. Confirm C-corp status and qualification at issuance. Owner: CFO tracks.
- [ ] Stand up the **cap table** as a real artifact (model it; do not just point at a location) → `Finance & Accounting (F&A)/Financials.md` or `Administration/`. Modeling the cap table is green; **changing the real cap table is red** (write-gate.md).
- [ ] Record **founding-state baseline** in `Overview.md` (entity, formation date, stage) and `Goals.md` (the first OKR set).

> Verify before it lands: the entity pack and the cap-table model are consequential. The Head of Quality verifies them against completion evidence before the skill persists them (verification.md). A producer never verifies its own work.

### 🚦 GATE 3 - Clean cap table and clocks set

- [ ] **Go:** entity formed, EIN and bank account live, IP assigned, founder stock issued, **83(b) filed within 30 days**, QSBS clock recorded, cap table clean. → opens **Equity**.
- [ ] **No-go / fix-first:** any open item, especially a missed or at-risk 83(b) window, before proceeding. A broken cap table or a missed 83(b) compounds with every later round.

Record to `Log.md`; note the gated actions the Founder confirmed.

---

## Stage 4 - EQUITY (split founders, set vesting, size the pool)

*Allocate ownership and align it to future contribution, not just to who showed up first. The equity split is one of the highest-regret decisions a founding team makes; vesting and a clean pool are the guardrails. Output: a founder split, standard vesting, an option pool, and the 409A baseline for option pricing.*

Convene: chair + CFO + General Counsel + CHRO on the option pool. All cap-table changes are **red / Founder-gated** (write-gate.md).

- [ ] Decide the **founder equity split** → `[founder: %]`. Anchor it to expected future contribution, role, and risk taken, not only to the idea or to time served. Document the rationale; an undocumented split is a future dispute.
- [ ] Apply **founder vesting** (standard: 4-year vest, 1-year cliff) so equity is earned over time and a departing founder does not walk with a dead-weight stake. Confirm this is the stock the 83(b) covers.
- [ ] Size the **employee option pool** → `[pool %]` (commonly ~10 to 20% reserved pre-Series-A). Note that investors usually require the pool be set **before** the round, diluting founders, so size it deliberately.
- [ ] Establish the **409A valuation** baseline so option strike prices are defensible.
- [ ] Confirm **83(b) elections are filed** for any restricted stock subject to vesting (re-check the Stage 3 clock; this is the last natural place to catch a miss).
- [ ] Record the equity structure into the **cap-table model**; keep the single canonical cap table as the source of truth.

### 🚦 GATE 4 - Aligned, vesting ownership

- [ ] **Go:** founder split agreed and documented, vesting in place, pool sized, 409A baseline set, 83(b) confirmed filed. → opens **GTM**.
- [ ] **Fix-first:** an unvested split, an undocumented rationale, or any unfiled 83(b). Resolve before adding the first hires or investors, who both make the cap table harder to change.

Record to `Log.md`.

---

## Stage 5 - GTM (founder-led first go-to-market)

*Prove you can repeatedly find and win a customer, by hand, before you try to systematize it. Early GTM is the founder selling, learning the motion, and writing down what works. The goal is a repeatable motion in embryo, not a scaled machine. Output: an ICP, a first positioning and message, an early channel that works, and the first real revenue.*

Convene: chair + CRO (the Chief Revenue Officer; the Product Marketing Manager on positioning, the Demand Generation Manager on channel) + CEO selling. Resist premature scaling: do not pour fuel on a motion that is not yet repeatable (lifecycle.md).

- [ ] Define the **ideal customer profile (ICP)** sharply → `[who, in one line]`. Narrow beats broad at this stage.
- [ ] Write **positioning and core message**: the why-now and the how-we-win, in the customer's words. File to `Sales & Marketing (S&M)/Brand.md`.
- [ ] Run **founder-led sales / outreach**: the founder closes the first deals personally and hears every objection unfiltered.
- [ ] Test **one or two channels** to first signal; kill what does not work fast. Do not build a multi-channel plan before one channel works.
- [ ] Land the **first paying customers** and record real revenue (now a real signal, where Stage 1 it was vanity).
- [ ] Capture the **emerging motion**: what consistently moves a prospect from interest to paid. This is the seed of the future sales playbook, not the playbook itself.

> The seam to watch (lifecycle.md): first dollars from non-repeatable, founder-led selling is still **FOUND**. A documented, repeatable, instrumented motion is the signal the venture is leaving FOUND for SCALE. Do not declare the motion repeatable before the evidence says so.

### 🚦 GATE 5 - A repeatable motion in sight

- [ ] **Go:** an ICP that converts, a message that lands, at least one channel showing signal, and real paying customers. → opens **Hire** (and unlocks the case for **Raise**). → may advance the operating stage toward SCALE on the record (lifecycle.md, stage detection).
- [ ] **Pivot:** customers buy but the wrong ones, or the channel does not repeat. Re-segment the ICP or change the channel before scaling spend.
- [ ] **No-go:** no repeatable path to a won customer. Return to MVP or Validate; do not hire or raise against a motion that does not work.

Record to `Log.md`.

---

## Stage 6 - HIRE (the first hire, only against a real bottleneck)

*Make the first hire only when the founders are the bottleneck on a validated motion, not to do work that is not yet repeatable. Premature hiring burns the scarce resource (runway) on an unproven motion. Output: a first key hire that unlocks the founders' highest-leverage time, with comp that fits the stage.*

Convene: chair + CHRO (the Chief Human Resources Officer, with sourcing and compensation seats spawned on demand) + the hiring function's lead. Any offer is a **red / Founder-gated** action (signing/sending a contract, write-gate.md): the team drafts the offer; the Founder sends it.

- [ ] Confirm the **bottleneck is real and named** → `[the specific work the founders can no longer hold]`. Hire to unlock founder leverage, not to offload a task that is not yet repeatable.
- [ ] Write the **role definition and the first 90-day success measure** before opening the search. File the hiring need to `Human Resources (HR)/` and the org context to `Hierarchy.md`.
- [ ] Set **stage-appropriate compensation**: lower cash, meaningful equity, against the option pool sized in Stage 4. Use the comp bands the CHRO sets.
- [ ] Run a **structured, evidence-based hiring process** (consistent questions, a work sample, references). One bad early hire is outsized at this size.
- [ ] Issue the **offer with equity from the pool**, vesting and (if restricted stock) an 83(b) reminder for the new hire. Owner: CHRO drafts; **Founder sends.**
- [ ] Plan **onboarding to first contribution**; the first hire sets the cultural baseline every later hire inherits.

> Stage check (lifecycle.md): hiring a function before its motion is repeatable is premature process and premature hiring at once. Hire behind proven leverage, not ahead of it.

### 🚦 GATE 6 - First leverage hire landed

- [ ] **Go:** a real bottleneck, a defined role and success measure, a stage-fit offer accepted, onboarding planned. → the venture can scale the team behind proven leverage.
- [ ] **No-go / wait:** the bottleneck is not yet real, or the motion is not yet repeatable. Hold the hire; protect runway.

Record to `Log.md`.

---

## Stage 7 - RAISE (only if the model needs venture capital)

*Raise outside capital only if the business genuinely needs it to reach the next milestone and the venture path fits the founders' intent (the LLC / cash-flow path may not raise at all). A raise sells future ownership; do it from a position of demonstrated traction, against a specific use of funds. Output: a clear raise decision, and if go, the round mechanics, the deck, and the milestone the money buys.*

Convene: chair + CFO + CEO (strategy hat) + General Counsel. The financing itself (terms, SAFEs, the round) is **red / Founder-gated** and trips the equity/cap-table gate; several items also touch the QSBS clock (write-gate.md).

- [ ] Decide **whether to raise at all** → `[raise | bootstrap]`. A capital-efficient or cash-flow business may not need it; raising dilutes ownership and resets expectations to a venture-scale outcome. This is a strategy decision, not a default.
- [ ] If raising, define the **milestone the round buys** → `[the specific milestone, e.g. repeatable motion at X scale]` and the **use of funds**. Investors fund a milestone, not a runway.
- [ ] Choose the **instrument** → `[SAFE | priced round | note]` and the **target amount and runway** it buys (commonly ~18 to 24 months). Confirm the C-corp structure supports it (SAFEs and priced rounds assume a C-corp; QSBS qualification persists if the C-corp conditions hold).
- [ ] Build the **forward financial model / projections** (3-statement, scenarios) and the **investor narrative / deck**: problem, why-now, traction, model, team, ask. File the model to `Finance & Accounting (F&A)/Financials.md`; drafting is green, but **sending the deck or signing terms is red.**
- [ ] Confirm **diligence readiness**: clean cap table, IP fully assigned, 83(b) filed, corporate records in order. The Stage 3 to 4 hygiene is what makes this stage fast.
- [ ] Note the **cap-table and QSBS impact** of the round before committing; a new issuance starts its own QSBS clock for the new shares.

### 🚦 GATE 7 - Raise decision (go / no-go / bootstrap)

- [ ] **Go (raise):** the business needs capital to hit a specific milestone, traction supports a credible story, diligence is clean. The Founder authorizes the terms (red action). → the venture moves into SCALE with funded runway.
- [ ] **Bootstrap:** the model reaches the next milestone without dilution. A valid, often superior, outcome. Record the choice and why.
- [ ] **No-go (not yet):** traction does not yet support a raise on good terms. Return to GTM, build the proof, raise later from strength.

Record to `Log.md`; any executed financing is a confirmed red action, logged with the Founder's confirmation noted.

---

## Closing the found run

When the gates have cleared and the venture has a working motion (and funded or bootstrapped runway), the venture has left **FOUND**. The chair:

- [ ] **Advances the operating stage** on the record toward SCALE when the signals warrant it (lifecycle.md, stage detection): a documented, repeatable, instrumented motion is the seam-breaker, not the round name. Update `Overview.md` and append to `Log.md` (green, autonomous; commit the prior state first).
- [ ] **Confirms both founding clocks are honored**: 83(b) filed within 30 days (closed, not pending), QSBS issuance date and 5-year maturity recorded and tracked by the CFO.
- [ ] **Hands off to strategize** to set the next stage's OKRs against the new motion (the SCALE-stage dominant question becomes: *is the founder the bottleneck, and is each channel actually efficient?*).
- [ ] **Files the founding record**: `Strategy.md` (thesis), the cap-table model, the entity pack, and the decision log of every gate, so the next run is not blind.

The throughline holds across all seven stages: one workforce scaled small for FOUND, every angle heard with one owner accountable, consequential output verified by the Head of Quality before it lands, and the skill as the sole writer behind the write-gate. The Founder alone authorizes the red actions, of which founding has the most of any mode: the entity, the equity, the offers, and the round. See write-gate.md for the autonomous-versus-gated line, verification.md for the verify-before-write discipline, lifecycle.md for the FOUND-stage doctrine, and deliberation.md for how to run each gate as a decision.

# OKR cycle - the scaffold for an annual-to-quarterly OKR ladder (strategize mode)

*The fill-in scaffold a strategize run uses to write the venture's OKRs into `Goals.md`: annual objectives at the top, the quarterly OKRs that ladder up to them below, each key result tagged committed or aspirational and carrying a 0.0-to-1.0 grading line. It connects the company thesis in `Strategy.md` to the north-star in `Metrics.md`, and it is the spine the four review loops grade against. Fill only the brackets the venture actually has; never fabricate a target.*

The chair fills this in a **strategize** run, then the skill writes the result into the venture's `Goals.md` behind the write-gate (see `write-gate.md`). The OKRs ladder up: a few annual objectives state what the year is for, and each quarter's OKRs are the slice of that year the venture commits to next. The ladder has to hold in both directions, every quarterly objective serves a named annual objective, and every annual objective is served by at least one live quarterly OKR, or the cycle has a gap. The north-star metric is not redefined here; it is canonical in `Metrics.md` (BI owns it) and referenced, so the OKRs and the scoreboard cannot drift apart. Stage-scale the whole cycle (`lifecycle.md`): a **found** venture writes few OKRs against learning and survival signals and grades loosely; a **scale** venture writes efficiency and repeatability OKRs and grades hard on the numbers; a **maintain** venture splits the ladder across Three Horizons so defending the core does not starve the next S-curve. Keep the standard: **every angle heard, one owner accountable**. Each objective and each key result has exactly one single-threaded owner, OKRs are set by catchball (the chair frames the target, the owning chief returns what is committable; see `operating-cadence.md`), and the skill is the sole writer.

---

## How to read this scaffold

- **Objective** is qualitative and directional: what success looks like, in a sentence a human would be proud to hit. It is not a metric.
- **Key result (KR)** is the measurable proof the objective moved: a number with a start, a target, and a date, so a grade is unambiguous at the QBR. If you cannot grade it 0.0 to 1.0 from data, it is a task, not a KR.
- **Owner** is one named person (one workforce chief or specialist), single-threaded. Two owners is no owner.
- **Tag** is `committed` or `aspirational`, defined below. The tag sets the bar the grade is read against.
- **Grade** is the 0.0-to-1.0 line, blank at planning, filled at the QBR. Carry the line from the start so grading is mechanical, not a renegotiation.

---

## Cycle header

- **Venture:** [name]
- **Stage:** [found / scale / maintain, from `Overview.md`, reconciled with the real signals per `lifecycle.md`]
- **Annual period:** [FY2026, or the fiscal year this ladder covers]
- **Quarter being set:** [Q_ 2026]
- **Thesis it serves:** [one line from `Strategy.md`: where we play and how we win this year]
- **North-star metric:** [the single metric, by reference to `Metrics.md`; current value and as-of date] - *canonical in `Metrics.md`, not redefined here*
- **Set by:** [the chair plus the chiefs whose functions own the KRs; catchball recorded]
- **Framework feeding this:** [the strategize output that produced the objectives, e.g. Balanced Scorecard, V2MOM at the annual tier; see `strategy-toolkit.md`]

---

## Committed vs aspirational (tag every KR)

Every key result carries one tag, and the tag is a promise about the bar, not a mood.

- **Committed.** A KR the venture is on the hook to fully deliver. The expected grade is **1.0**; anything less is a miss that needs a reason and usually a recovery plan. Resource it as if failure is not an option, because that is the commitment. Use it sparingly, for the load-bearing few (runway, a shipped launch, a contractual or survival number).
- **Aspirational.** A stretch KR set deliberately beyond comfortable reach. The expected grade is **~0.7** on the Google convention: consistently scoring 1.0 means the bar was set too low (sandbagged), and consistently scoring below 0.3 means it was fantasy. Aspirational OKRs are where real ambition lives; they are graded generously and missing one is information, not failure.

Do not blur the two. A quarter that is all-committed is a venture not reaching; a quarter that is all-aspirational is a venture with nothing it can be held to. Most quarters carry a small committed core and a larger aspirational stretch, and the split itself is a stage decision: **found** leans aspirational against learning, **scale** holds a hard committed efficiency core, **maintain** commits the core defense and aspires on the H2/H3 bets.

---

## The grading line (0.0 to 1.0)

Each KR carries a grading line, written at planning and scored at the QBR (`operating-cadence.md`, Loop 3). The score is the fraction of the target achieved, clamped to [0.0, 1.0], read against the KR's tag.

```
KR grade = clamp( (final - start) / (target - start), 0.0, 1.0 )
```

- **Committed** target the score at **1.0**. A committed KR landing at 0.6 is a real miss, not a near-pass.
- **Aspirational** target the score at **~0.7**. A 0.7 on a true stretch is a good quarter; do not treat it as a 70% failure.
- **The objective's score** is the mean (or a stated weighting) of its KRs, reported alongside a one-line *why* for each, learning not excuse.
- A KR that cannot be scored from data at the QBR was mis-written; fix the KR, do not argue the grade.

Leave the score blank at planning. At the QBR the verifier checks the grades against the evidence before the skill writes them back (a function does not grade its own OKR unchecked; see `verification.md`), and the regraded closing OKRs plus the new quarter's OKRs are written into `Goals.md`.

---

## Annual objectives (the top of the ladder)

The few things the whole year is for. Each quarterly OKR below must ladder up to one of these. Annual objectives are usually qualitative with one or two annual measures (the V2MOM "Measures" line; see `operating-cadence.md`, Loop 4); the quarters carry the gradeable detail.

### Annual Objective A: [the qualitative outcome, in one line]

- **Why this year:** [the thesis link: why this objective is what the year turns on]
- **Annual measure(s):** [the one or two numbers that prove the year delivered it, with target and as-of]
- **Owner (annual):** [the one accountable chief]
- **Three Horizons:** [H1 defend / H2 build / H3 seed - only at scale and maintain, where the ladder is split across horizons per `lifecycle.md`]

### Annual Objective B: [...]

- **Why this year:** [...]
- **Annual measure(s):** [...]
- **Owner (annual):** [...]
- **Three Horizons:** [...]

### Annual Objective C: [...]

- **Why this year:** [...]
- **Annual measure(s):** [...]
- **Owner (annual):** [...]
- **Three Horizons:** [...]

> Keep annual objectives to roughly three to five. More than five is not a strategy, it is a wish list, and the quarters cannot serve them all.

---

## Quarterly OKRs (the gradeable slice)

The quarter being set. Each objective names the annual objective it ladders up to. Each KR carries an owner, a committed-or-aspirational tag, and the start to target to grade line. Set by catchball and recorded so the next QBR grades against what was actually agreed.

### Objective 1: [the qualitative quarterly outcome]

- **Ladders up to:** [Annual Objective A / B / C]
- **Owner (objective):** [one accountable chief]

| # | Key result | Owner | Tag | Start | Target | By | Grade (0.0-1.0) |
|---|------------|-------|-----|-------|--------|----|-----------------|
| KR1 | [measurable result, a number] | [name] | committed / aspirational | [baseline] | [target] | [date] | [blank at planning] |
| KR2 | [...] | [name] | committed / aspirational | [...] | [...] | [...] |  |
| KR3 | [...] | [name] | committed / aspirational | [...] | [...] | [...] |  |

- **Objective grade (at QBR):** [mean or stated weighting of the KR grades]
- **Why (one line each at QBR):** [hit / missed / de-scoped, and the reason, learning not excuse]

### Objective 2: [...]

- **Ladders up to:** [...]
- **Owner (objective):** [...]

| # | Key result | Owner | Tag | Start | Target | By | Grade (0.0-1.0) |
|---|------------|-------|-----|-------|--------|----|-----------------|
| KR1 | [...] | [...] | committed / aspirational | [...] | [...] | [...] |  |
| KR2 | [...] | [...] | committed / aspirational | [...] | [...] | [...] |  |

- **Objective grade (at QBR):** [...]
- **Why:** [...]

### Objective 3: [...]

- **Ladders up to:** [...]
- **Owner (objective):** [...]

| # | Key result | Owner | Tag | Start | Target | By | Grade (0.0-1.0) |
|---|------------|-------|-----|-------|--------|----|-----------------|
| KR1 | [...] | [...] | committed / aspirational | [...] | [...] | [...] |  |
| KR2 | [...] | [...] | committed / aspirational | [...] | [...] | [...] |  |

- **Objective grade (at QBR):** [...]
- **Why:** [...]

> Keep it to roughly three objectives with two to four KRs each. A quarter with eight objectives has no priorities. Over-scoping the quarter is the most common OKR failure, and it shows up as a wall of 0.4 grades the venture explains away.

---

## Ladder check (do not skip)

Before the skill writes this into `Goals.md`, confirm the ladder holds both ways:

- **Up:** every quarterly objective names exactly one annual objective it serves. No orphans.
- **Down:** every annual objective is served by at least one live quarterly OKR this quarter, or it is explicitly parked with a reason. No dead annual objectives.
- **North-star:** at least one KR moves, or directly protects, the north-star metric in `Metrics.md`. If nothing in the quarter touches the north-star, the quarter is busywork, not progress.
- **Owners:** every objective and every KR has exactly one named owner. Zero unowned, zero double-owned.
- **Tags:** every KR is tagged. The committed core is small and survival-or-contract critical; the rest is aspirational. The split matches the stage.
- **Gradeability:** every KR has a start, a target, and a date, so its 0.0-to-1.0 grade will be mechanical at the QBR.

---

## Where this lands and how it is graded

- **Written to:** the venture's `Goals.md` (the OKRs ladder lives there), by the skill, behind the write-gate, with the existing file's last state committed first. The annual objectives are the top of `Goals.md`; the quarterly OKRs are the current cycle.
- **Grounded in:** `Strategy.md` (the thesis the objectives serve) and `Metrics.md` (the canonical north-star and KPIs; the OKRs reference it, never redefine it).
- **Graded by:** the quarterly QBR (`operating-cadence.md`, Loop 3): each KR scored 0.0 to 1.0 against its tag, the verifier checks the grades (`verification.md`), the chair synthesizes, and the regraded closing OKRs plus the next quarter's OKRs are written back to `Goals.md` with a dated `Log.md` entry.
- **Reset by:** catchball at the QBR and annual planning (`operating-cadence.md`, Loop 4, V2MOM at the annual tier). The next ladder is set against the grades this one earned, so honest grading now is what makes the next cycle realistic.

> The OKR ladder is the one artifact every review loop reads: the weekly loop checks rocks against it, the monthly loop checks mid-quarter pace against it, the quarterly loop grades and resets it, the annual loop sets the objectives it ladders up to. Set it once, well, and the cadence runs on it. Set it loosely, and every loop inherits the slack.

# Board and QBR six-pager

*A written, prose pre-read for the quarterly board meeting and the internal quarterly business review: a narrative, not slides. Page 1 opens with the recommendation and the asks; the outward BOARD UPDATE (governance, financials, runway, the asks the Founder must answer) is separated from the inward QBR (last quarter's OKR grades, the next 90 days, the trade-offs). Filed to the venture's `Administration/` by the review mode behind the write-gate, with the Head of Quality verifying every number against a tool or source first (see verification.md, write-gate.md). The skill is the sole writer; agents compose and return.*

This template scaffolds the **review** mode's quarterly deliverable. The review run reads the venture's `Overview.md`, `Goals.md`, `Strategy.md`, and recent `Log.md`, detects the stage (see lifecycle.md), grades the quarter's OKRs, and assembles this six-pager. The CFO and the FP&A Analyst own the financial pages; the Corporate Secretary composes the governance record; the CEO holds the synthesis and states the recommendation; the Head of Quality verifies before the skill persists. One owner is named on every ask and every objective. The standard holds: **every angle heard, one owner accountable**.

## How to use this scaffold

- **Write prose, not bullets-as-slides.** This is a Bezos-style six-pager: full sentences and paragraphs, read in silence at the top of the meeting. The tables here are for the financial and OKR data only; the surrounding analysis is narrative. A reader who only had this document, and never the meeting, should understand the state of the company and the decisions in front of it.
- **Recommendation first.** Page 1 leads with the headline and the asks. Do not bury the recommendation on page 4. The reader learns what you want them to conclude, then reads the case for it.
- **Two audiences, one document, kept separate.** Pages 1 to 3 are the **outward board update** (what owners and directors govern and oversee: financials, runway, governance, the asks). Pages 4 to 6 are the **inward QBR** (how the team ran the company: OKR grades, the next 90 days, the trade-offs being made). Do not blend them; a director reads the first half, the operating team lives in the second.
- **Stage-scale the document.** A found-stage venture leads with PMF evidence, learning velocity, and runway; suppress Rule of 40 and the Magic Number as not-yet-applicable (see metrics-and-kpis.md). A scale-stage venture leads with unit economics and efficiency (CAC payback, NRR, burn multiple). A maintain-stage venture leads with durability and the next S-curve (Rule of 40, FCF, H2/H3 pipeline). Grey out, or drop, any metric not yet load-bearing for the stage rather than reporting a vanity number.
- **Ground every number in a source.** Each financial figure and each OKR grade carries its source (the model, the close, the dashboard, the metric definition). The Head of Quality verifies the document against those sources before the skill writes it; an unverifiable number does not ship (see verification.md).
- **One owner per ask and per objective.** Every ask resolves to a single decider (CEO for in-mandate calls, Founder for the irreversible or major ones), and every objective has one accountable owner. No ask is addressed to "the board" in general.
- **Delete the prompts.** Bracketed text is instruction. Replace it, and remove any section that does not apply to this venture at this stage rather than leaving it empty.

Fill whatever frontmatter the venture's `Administration/` files use under the repository's instructions (real values, no `[Company]` placeholder, links in the repository's own convention); this scaffold below the title is plain payload.

---

# [Venture] - Board update and Q[n] [YYYY] review

**Prepared by:** [CEO, with CFO on the financials and Corporate Secretary on the record]   **For:** [the board / the Founder as chair]   **Quarter:** Q[n] [YYYY] ([start date] to [end date])   **Stage:** [found / scale / maintain, per lifecycle.md]   **Verified by:** [Head of Quality, date]

---

## Page 1 - The recommendation and the asks (read this first)

> [!TIP]
> **The headline.**
> [One paragraph. The single most important thing the reader must take away from this quarter, stated as a conclusion, not a teaser. What the company is, where it stands against its thesis, what the quarter proved or disproved, and what you are recommending the board do or approve. If a director read only this paragraph, they would know the state of the company and what is being asked of them.]

**The quarter in one line:** [the result, the way you would say it out loud: "we hit X, missed Y, and the riskiest open question is now Z."]

**The asks.** [Each ask is a specific decision or approval the board or the Founder must make, with the one decider named and the consequence of a yes and a no. Order by what is gating. Asks that need money, a contract, external comms, a delete, or a change to equity or the cap table are hard-gated to the Founder; route them here and do not act on them inside this run (see write-gate.md).]

| # | The ask | Decider | Why now / what it unblocks | Recommended answer |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | [the specific decision or approval] | [Founder / CEO] | [the gating reason and the consequence] | [your recommendation] |
| 2 | [the specific decision or approval] | [Founder / CEO] | [the gating reason and the consequence] | [your recommendation] |

**What is going well, what is at risk, what changed since last quarter.** [Three short paragraphs or a tight list. The wins worth defending, the risks worth the board's attention, and the one or two things that are materially different from the last board meeting. Name the trend, not just the snapshot.]

---

## Page 2 - Financials, runway, and the plan-versus-actual (outward)

*Owner: CFO, with the FP&A Analyst on the model and the Controller on the close. Every figure ties to the financial model, the close package, or `Financials.md`; the source is named.*

**Cash and runway (the survival number).** [Cash on hand, monthly net burn, and runway in months at current burn, then at planned burn. State the date the company runs out of money under each case and what the plan is to extend it. This is the number a board reads first; lead the page with it.]

| Metric | This quarter (actual) | Plan | Prior quarter | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cash on hand | [$] | [$] | [$] | [model / close] |
| Net monthly burn | [$] | [$] | [$] | [model / close] |
| Runway (months) | [n] | [n] | [n] | [derived] |
| Revenue [/ ARR / MRR] | [$] | [$] | [$] | [close / dashboard] |
| Gross margin | [%] | [%] | [%] | [close] |
| [stage-relevant headline: Rule of 40 / NRR / burn multiple / CAC payback] | [value] | [value] | [value] | [definition] |

**Plan versus actual, and why the variance.** [Narrative. Walk the material variances against the operating plan: what beat, what missed, and the cause of each, not just the size. A variance with no explanation is a flag, not a report. Distinguish a timing variance from a structural one.]

**Stage-relevant unit economics.** [For a scale or maintain venture: CAC, LTV, LTV:CAC, CAC payback, NRR, burn multiple, against their 2025/26 benchmark bands (see metrics-and-kpis.md), each statused. For a found venture: state explicitly that unit economics are not yet load-bearing and report the learning and activation metrics instead. Do not report a metric the stage has not earned.]

**The forward look.** [The next-quarter and next-12-month projection in a sentence or two: the trajectory, the key assumption it rests on, and the point at which the company must raise, cut, or change course. Tie this to the asks on Page 1.]

---

## Page 3 - Governance, risk, and the corporate record (outward)

*Owner: Corporate Secretary for the record, General Counsel for legal and compliance, with the relevant chief on each risk. The Corporate Secretary composes; the skill writes.*

**Decisions of record this quarter.** [The board-level and major management decisions made since the last meeting, each as a one-line entry: the call, the decider, the date, and a pointer to its decision memo in `Administration/Decisions.md`. This is the governance trail; it ties this six-pager to the decisions behind it.]

**Governance and compliance status.** [Entity, cap-table, and filing status in brief: anything the board must ratify, any consent needed, any deadline approaching. Surface the irreversible clocks where they apply: the 83(b) 30-day window and the QSBS 5-year clock for a recently incorporated venture (see founding-playbook.md). Note any open legal or regulatory exposure and its owner.]

**The risk register (top risks, owned).** [The handful of enterprise risks that warrant board attention, each rated by likelihood and impact, with a named owner and the current mitigation. This is the inward-facing pre-mortem made visible to the board; do not launder a real risk into a reassurance.]

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Owner | Mitigation / status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [the risk] | [H/M/L] | [H/M/L] | [chief] | [what is being done] |
| [the risk] | [H/M/L] | [H/M/L] | [chief] | [what is being done] |

---

## Page 4 - Last quarter's OKRs, graded (inward)

*Owner: CEO, grading against `Goals.md`. Grades are 0.0 to 1.0; committed objectives are expected to land near 1.0, aspirational ones near 0.7. Grade honestly: a board that only ever sees green learns nothing, and a sandbagged 1.0 is as useless as a missed commitment.*

**The grades.** [Each objective and its key results, with the numeric grade, the actual-versus-target, and a one-line "what the grade means." Tag each objective committed or aspirational so a 0.6 on an aspirational moonshot is not read as a 0.6 on a commitment.]

| Objective | Type | Key result | Target | Actual | Grade (0.0-1.0) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [O1] | [committed / aspirational] | [KR] | [target] | [actual] | [0.0-1.0] |
| | | [KR] | [target] | [actual] | [0.0-1.0] |
| [O2] | [committed / aspirational] | [KR] | [target] | [actual] | [0.0-1.0] |

**What the grades mean, in prose.** [The narrative behind the numbers. Which objectives we hit and why, which we missed and why, and what we now know that we did not at the start of the quarter. Separate a miss caused by a wrong bet from a miss caused by poor execution; they call for different responses. Name the single biggest learning of the quarter.]

**What we are stopping.** [The work, the experiment, or the bet we are explicitly ending because the quarter disproved it or deprioritized it. A QBR that only adds and never stops is not making real trade-offs. Name what dies so the next 90 days have room.]

---

## Page 5 - The next 90 days (inward)

*Owner: CEO, with the COO on the execution plan. These objectives become the venture's `Goals.md` for the coming quarter; this page is the catchball, not a fait accompli.*

**The dominant question for the quarter.** [One sentence. The single question this quarter exists to answer, scaled to the stage: for found, "is there real evidence of PMF?"; for scale, "is the founder the bottleneck, and is each channel actually efficient?"; for maintain, "is the core defended and is there a funded next S-curve?" (see lifecycle.md). Everything below should ladder up to this.]

**Next quarter's OKRs.** [Three to five objectives, each with two to four measurable key results, each tagged committed or aspirational, each with one accountable owner. These ladder up to the thesis in `Strategy.md` and the dominant question above. Set them as catchball: the team proposes, the chair and Founder shape, the owner commits.]

| Objective | Type | Owner | Key results (measurable) |
|---|---|---|---|
| [O1] | [committed / aspirational] | [single owner] | [KR / KR / KR] |
| [O2] | [committed / aspirational] | [single owner] | [KR / KR / KR] |
| [O3] | [committed / aspirational] | [single owner] | [KR / KR / KR] |

**The plan to deliver them.** [Short narrative. The handful of bets and workstreams that move these objectives, who owns each, and the sequencing where one gates another. This is the COO's execution plan in prose, not a Gantt chart. Name the one or two things that, if they slip, put the quarter at risk.]

---

## Page 6 - The trade-offs and the bets (inward)

*Owner: CEO, wearing the strategy hat on the trade-offs. This is the page that earns the document: the honest case for where the company is choosing to spend its finite attention and capital, and what it is choosing not to do.*

**The central trade-off this quarter.** [Prose. The real fork the company faces: the two or three things it could pour the next quarter into and the one it is choosing, with the cost of that choice named. State the road not taken and why. A QBR without a visible trade-off is hiding the decision, not making it.]

**Resource allocation and the horizon mix.** [Where the quarter's capital and attention go, framed by the Three-Horizons split appropriate to the stage (roughly 100/0/0 at found, 70/20/10 at scale and maintain; see lifecycle.md). For a maintain venture, make the case that H2 and H3 are funded and not starved by the defended core. Name the bet that, if it pays off, changes the company.]

**The pre-mortem: how this quarter fails.** [Write the failure story a quarter out, then the mitigations. The ways the plan on Page 5 does not happen, ranked by likelihood, each with what would catch it early and who owns watching for it. This is the inward counterpart to the risk register on Page 3, in the team's own voice.]

**The minority view.** [The dissent, by role and reason, on the recommendation and the plan. Present even when the call is confident. A quarter's plan with no recorded dissent usually means it was smoothed over in the room, not that everyone genuinely agreed (see deliberation.md). Record who disagreed and on what, so the next QBR can check who was right.]

---

*Filed by the review mode to `Administration/` and summarized in `Log.md`; the OKRs on Page 5 are written into `Goals.md` and the stage on `Overview.md` is advanced or flagged if the quarter changed it. Money, contracts, external comms, deletes, and equity in the asks are routed to the Founder, never executed inside this run (see write-gate.md).*
